item.title: [github_trending] debpalash/VoiceStudio
item.description: VoiceStudio is an open-source, fully local alternative to ElevenLabs, bundling voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation across 646 languages. It ships as a downloadable app with documentation and a Discord community, aimed at developers and creators who want these capabilities without routing audio through a third-party cloud service.

item.title: [producthunt] MCP Connectors by Databox
item.description: Databox launched MCP Connectors on Product Hunt, wiring external data sources into its AI Analyst over MCP so the assistant has the business context needed to explain performance and take action. Teams already running Databox dashboards that want an AI reasoning over their own data are the intended users.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A Juejin author writes up roughly half a month of moving from Cursor to Codex, saying Cursor was the first thing that made AI coding feel striking, while Codex comes across not as a coding assistant but as a genuine super agent, closer to the next stage of the form. Developers weighing the two tools, or wondering what agent-style coding feels like day to day, are the audience.

item.title: [infoq] Cloudflare 推出智能体开发栈生命周期，以取代传统 SDLC
item.description: Cloudflare has proposed an Agent Development Lifecycle to replace the traditional SDLC, arguing that once AI accelerates code generation, testing, deployment and maintenance become the bottleneck. The design gives every agent its own preview deployment, enforces atomic changes, and uses Cloudflare Workflows as the orchestration layer, with a new @cloudflare/ci tool running on top. It targets platform teams putting autonomous agents into their pipelines.

item.title: [infoq] Agent 编程能力从 10% 飙到 70%，Anthropic 新模型却遭遇灵魂拷问：我什么时候才会用它？
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family, claiming over 30% faster output and up to 30% lower cost per task. It jumped from 10.3% to 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, beating Opus 5.5's published best, while early testers report roughly a third fewer tool calls and about half the shell executions. Base44 measured an average of 3.6 iterations per app build against 7.7 for Opus 5, which matters to teams running coding agents such as Claude Code.

Teams building LLM agents that need durable, searchable long-term memory can evaluate it as an off-the-shelf component.
